definition.name: Fan Membership Platform
definition.overview:
A **Fan Membership Platform** is an application that lets fans become paying members of a specific creator's membership program: the fan pays recurring dues, holds a member standing in that creator's program, and receives the benefits the membership declares for as long as the membership stays active.

The defining core is small:

```text
Creator's membership program (fan club)
└── Membership plan / level (dues + declared member benefits)
    └── Membership (fan's standing enrollment, recurring dues)
        └── Member benefits (granted while active, ended on lapse/cancel)
```

If any of these is removed, the product stops being a fan membership platform: without recurring dues it is one-time support (a tip); without a specific creator as the counterparty it is an organization's membership system or a media catalog subscription; without creator-authored plans it is a platform-defined subscription; without standing benefits it is a goods purchase.

Mature products in this category commonly add tier ladders, free plans, members-only content, community roles, gamified participation, capacity limits, and regional payment options — these are standard capabilities, not the definition. Older and regional realizations (a postal-era fan club collecting annual dues and mailing a member newsletter) satisfy the core with none of them.

The category sits next to **Creator Subscription Platform**, and the market often uses "membership" and "subscription" interchangeably for the same recurring fan→creator structure. The distinction this document maintains is one of center of gravity: subscription platforms foreground the recurring payment relationship and the creator's gated output stream (typically publishing-shaped products); fan membership platforms foreground the fan's belonging to a creator's program — joining, member standing, declared benefits, and the member's participation around the creator. In practice most products exhibit both emphases at once; see Related Application Types.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**粉丝会员平台**是一种应用程序，让粉丝成为特定创作者会员计划的付费会员：粉丝支付定期会费，在该创作者的计划中持有会员身份，并只要会员保持活跃状态，就能获得会员计划所宣布的权益。

其定义性核心很简单：

```text
创作者的会员计划（粉丝俱乐部）
└── 会员计划/等级（会费 + 宣布的会员权益）
    └── 会员（粉丝的身份登记，定期会费）
        └── 会员权益（活跃期间授予，过期/取消时终止）
```

如果缺少其中任何一项，产品就不再是粉丝会员平台：没有定期会费，它就是一次性支持（小费）；没有特定创作者作为对手方，它就是组织的会员系统或媒体目录订阅；没有创作者制定的计划，它就是平台定义的订阅；没有持续权益，它就是商品购买。

此类别中的成熟产品通常会添加等级阶梯、免费计划、仅会员内容、社区角色、游戏化参与、容量限制和区域支付选项——这些是标准能力，而非定义。较旧和区域实现（例如邮政时代的粉丝俱乐部，收取年费并邮寄会员通讯）即使没有这些也满足核心。

该类别与**创作者订阅平台**相邻，市场通常对相同的定期粉丝→创作者结构互换使用"会员"和"订阅"。本文档所维护的区别是重心不同：订阅平台以定期支付关系和创作者的受限输出流（通常是出版形式的产品）为重点；粉丝会员平台以粉丝对创作者计划的归属感为重点——加入、会员身份、宣布的权益以及成员在创作者周围的参与。实际上，大多数产品同时体现这两种重点；参见相关应用类型。
definition.dc:
**1. The membership program (fan club) — the container.**
Each creator operates one membership program: a persistent, branded space (a page, a club) that presents the program to fans and holds its plans, its member roster, and its member-only output. The counterparty is always a specific creator (or creator entity), never a platform catalog and never an unrelated business. The fan *joins* the program; the vocabulary of belonging — joining, membership, members, the club — is native to this Type.

**2. The membership plan / level — the offer.**
The creator defines what can be joined: a named plan or level carrying a dues amount and a declared set of member benefits. Common benefits include access to members-only posts and media, member-limited merchandise, community roles or badges, behind-the-scenes material, early or exclusive access, and physical or experiential perks. A program can be a single plan — the tier ladder with a price–perk gradient is the common shape in mature products, but one-plan programs are fully first-class. Dues typically recur monthly or yearly; some products add annual-upfront or other cadences.

**3. The membership — the fan's standing enrollment.**
When a fan joins a plan, the platform creates a standing membership: an ongoing entitlement that renews automatically until cancelled or until payment fails. The membership is stateful — active, suspended (payment issues or program pause), cancelled or expired — and member standing follows that state. Joining also establishes the fan's identity in the program's roster.

**4. Member standing and benefits — the state-linked entitlement.**
While the membership is active, the fan holds the plan's declared benefits. In practice the most common benefit is continuous access to the creator's member-limited output (posts, media, archives) and member-limited purchasing; in the purest support-framed programs, the standing itself (being a named supporter of the creator) plus whatever perks the plan declares. Benefits are granted on joining, maintained across renewals, and end when the membership lapses or is cancelled — typically with access preserved to the end of the paid period, or with a defined grace window.

**5. Creator-side membership management.**
The creator operates the program through an application surface: author and edit plans, view and work the member roster (inspect a member, grant complimentary memberships, cancel a membership on request), communicate with members or member groups, and receive earnings (platform-managed payouts, or settlement into the creator's own payment account depending on the product). Without this surface the product would be a payment processor, not an application.
definition.dc_zh: 1. 会员计划（粉丝俱乐部）——容器。每个创作者运营一个会员计划：一个持久的、品牌化的空间（页面、俱乐部），向粉丝展示该计划，并持有其计划、成员名册和仅限成员的输出。对手总是一个特定的创作者（或创作者实体），永远不是平台目录或不相关的业务。粉丝加入该计划；归属词汇——加入、会员、成员、俱乐部——是这个类型的原生词汇。2. 会员计划/等级——提议。创作者定义可加入的内容：一个命名的计划或等级，带有费用金额和一套声明的会员福利。常见福利包括访问仅限成员的帖子和媒体、成员限量商品、社区角色或徽章、幕后材料、早期或独家访问、以及实体或体验性特权。计划可以是单一计划——带有价格-福利梯度的分层结构是成熟产品中的常见形状，但单一计划也完全是一等公民。费用通常是每月或每年重复；有些产品添加年付或其他周期。3. 会员资格——粉丝的持久注册。当粉丝加入一个计划时，平台创建一个持久的会员资格：一个持续的权利，自动续订直到取消或支付失败。会员资格是有状态的——活跃、暂停（暂停）。
definition.rules:
- **Benefits follow membership state.** Cancelling stops future renewals, not current-period access; lapsing (expiry or failed payment) ends member-limited access. Exact edge timing (period end vs grace window) varies by product.
- **Dues auto-renew until cancelled or failed.** Renewal is the default posture; members opt out rather than opt in. Renewal charges usually notify the member.
- **Price changes protect existing members.** Whether by explicit grandfathering or by uneditable plan prices (delete-and-recreate to change pricing), the market-wide posture is that a member's dues stay as signed up unless they or the creator end the membership.
- **Comps are a creator power.** Creators can grant complimentary or time-limited memberships; some creators can also cancel a membership directly from the roster.
- **Capacity is optional and product-shaped.** Where offered, member limits create exclusivity or manage workload; a full plan shows a closed/recruitment-ended state until the creator raises the limit.
- **Fan privacy is structural.** The platform mediates the relationship: the fan's email and payment details generally do not reach the creator. The common exception is physical-goods fulfillment, where shipping details must pass.
- **Feature presence is not the boundary.** The same account commonly sells tips, goods, or commissions alongside memberships; what makes the membership is the standing enrollment with recurring dues and state-linked benefits, not any single feature.
definition.rules_zh:
- **权益跟随会员状态。** 取消停止未来续订，而非当前期间访问；过期（过期或支付失败）结束仅会员访问。确切的边界时间（期间结束 vs 宽限期）因产品而异。
- **会费自动续订直到取消或失败。** 续订是默认姿态；会员选择退出而非加入。续订收费通常通知会员。
- **价格变更保护现有会员。** 无论是通过明确的祖父条款还是通过不可编辑的计划价格（删除并重新创建以更改定价），市场普遍的姿态是会员的会费保持签约时的价格，除非他们或创作者结束会员资格。
- **免费赠送是创作者的权力。** 创作者可以授予免费或限时会员资格；一些创作者也可以直接从名册中取消会员资格。
- **容量是可选的且产品决定的。** 在提供时，会员限制创造排他性或管理工作负载；满员计划显示关闭/招募结束状态，直到创作者提高限制。
- **粉丝隐私是结构性的。** 平台调解关系：粉丝的电子邮件和支付详细信息通常不会到达创作者。常见的例外是实物商品履行，其中必须传递发货详细信息。
- **功能存在不是边界。** 同一账户通常同时销售小费、商品或佣金以及会员资格；使会员资格成立的是具有定期会费和状态相关权益的持续登记，而不是任何单一功能。

definition.name: Paid Community Platform
definition.overview:
A **Paid Community Platform** is software for running a community whose admission is organized by payment: the community host prices access to the venue, buyers join through checkout, and member access follows the state of that payment.

The defining structure is small:

```text
Community venue (hosted, participatory member spaces)
└── Purchase offer on admission (host-authored plan / pricing)
    └── Completed purchase → member access
        └── Access maintained while payment is active
            └── Access ends or degrades when payment lapses
```

Everything commonly associated with these products — free plans inside paid venues, tiered benefits, trials, courses, events, chat, gamification, landing pages, mobile apps — is widespread but is not what makes the product a paid community platform. A free, open community with no purchase offer is a community platform; a subscription to a creator's output stream with no participatory venue is a creator subscription. This Type sits precisely where the two overlap: the thing being sold is **access to a place where members participate**.
definition.overview_zh:
**付费社区平台**是一种用于运营社区的软件，其准入通过支付行为组织：社区主办方为场地访问权定价，买家通过结账流程加入，成员的访问权限则取决于该支付状态。

其定义性结构非常简洁：

```text
社区场地（托管的、成员可参与的互动空间）
└── 准入购买选项（主办方制定的计划/定价）
    └── 完成购买 → 获得成员访问权限
        └── 支付有效期间持续维持访问权限
            └── 支付到期后访问权限终止或降级
```

所有通常与这些产品相关联的功能——付费场地内的免费计划、分级权益、试用期、课程、活动、聊天、游戏化、落地页、移动应用——虽然普遍，但并非使其成为付费社区平台的核心要素。一个没有购买选项的免费、开放社区是社区平台；一个没有互动场地的创作者作品流订阅是创作者订阅。这一类型恰好处于两者重叠之处：所销售的是**进入一个成员可参与的场所的权限**。
definition.dc:
Four structures. If any one is removed, the product stops being recognizable as a paid community platform:

- **The paid venue** — a hosted community container with participatory member spaces (discussions, feed, chat, events, courses, member directory — the mix varies by product). The venue itself is the product being sold; it is not an add-on to something else.
- **Purchase offers on admission** — the host authors named offers (plans/pricing) that define what a buyer pays and what that payment covers. An offer attaches to the whole venue, to an individual space, or to a bundle of spaces. Recurring payment is typical; one-time payment for permanent or fixed-term access is common.
- **Payment-state-linked access** — a completed purchase converts the buyer into a member with immediate access to what the offer covered. Access persists across renewals and ends or degrades when payment does: cancellation takes effect at the end of the billing period, failed payment can deactivate the plan, and the host can revoke or grant access manually (refund, comp, removal).
- **Host-side monetization management** — the operator surface that makes the offer and its access consequences manageable: offer authoring, a member/purchaser roster, billing operations (cancel, comp, refund, price changes), and revenue disposition (payouts, platform fees, tax handling per the platform's money posture).

The third structure is the one that organizes everything else: the purchase is not a donation or a content download; it converts into a **standing entitlement to a place**.
definition.dc_zh: 四个结构：1. 付费场地 — 一个托管的社区容器，带有参与式成员空间（讨论、动态、聊天、活动、课程、成员目录——混合因产品而异）。场地本身是被销售的产品；它不是其他东西的附加品。2. 入场购买报价 — 主持人创作的命名报价（计划/定价），定义买家支付什么以及支付覆盖什么。报价附加到整个场地、单个空间或一组空间。定期支付是典型的；一次性支付永久或固定期限访问也很常见。3. 支付状态链接访问 — 完成购买将买家转换为成员，并立即获得报价覆盖内容的访问权限。访问在续订时持续，当支付未完成时结束或降级：取消在计费期结束时生效，支付失败可以停用计划，主持人可以手动撤销或授予访问权限（退款、赠送、移除）。4. 主持人侧变现管理 — 操作员界面，使报价及其访问后果可管理：报价创作、成员/买家名册、计费操作（取消、赠送、退款、价格更改）和收入分配（支付、平台费用、税务处理，根据平台的资金立场）。
definition.rules:
- **Access follows payment, not attendance or activity.** A lapsed payment — not a rule violation, not inactivity — is what ends an entitlement (rule violations are handled separately through moderation).
- **Cancellation is not immediate expulsion.** The standard behavior is access until the end of the paid period; immediate removal is reserved for host action (removal, refund-with-revoke) or member account deletion.
- **Payment is the primary gate, but not the only one.** Screening questions and approval gates are commonly layered onto a paid offer; invite-only and hidden (link-only) offers exist for private sales.
- **The scope of the offer defines the entitlement.** Whole-venue offers grant full membership; space-scoped offers grant a limited membership whose capabilities are visibly narrower (for example, reduced venue-wide messaging or search).
- **Price changes typically protect existing members.** Grandfathering — new members pay the new price, existing members keep the price they joined at — is the commonly documented pattern.
- **Refunds and comps are host-discretionary.** The platform usually processes the money but leaves the refund decision and execution to the host; where app-store purchases are involved, refunds route through the app store instead.
- **One-time offers create durable access.** A one-time purchase does not lapse; it ends only by host action or account deletion, which is why one-time and recurring offers coexist as distinct choices rather than a single model.
definition.rules_zh:
- **访问权限遵循支付，而非出勤或活跃度。** 导致权限终止的是支付到期——而非规则违规或不活跃——（规则违规通过单独的版面管理处理）。
- **取消并非立即驱逐。** 标准行为是访问权限持续到付费期结束；立即移除保留给主办方操作（移除、退款并撤销）或成员账户删除。
- **支付是主要门槛，但非唯一门槛。** 筛选问题和审批门槛常叠加在付费选项之上；仅限邀请和隐藏（仅限链接）选项用于私密销售。
- **选项的范围界定权限内容。** 全场选项授予完整会员资格；限定于特定空间的选项授予能力范围明显更窄的有限会员资格（例如，全场范围内的消息或搜索功能受限）。
- **价格变更通常保护现有成员。** 祖父条款——新成员支付新价格，现有成员保留加入时的价格——是常见且明确的模式。
- **退款和赠送由主办方酌情决定。** 平台通常处理资金，但退款决定和执行交由主办方；若涉及应用商店购买，退款则通过应用商店进行。
- **一次性购买选项创建持久访问权限。** 一次性购买不会到期；仅通过主办方操作或账户删除终止，这是一次性与循环性选项作为不同选择而非单一模式并存的原因。

definition.name: Author Management Platform
definition.overview:
An **Author Management Platform** is publisher-side software for managing a publishing organization's ongoing relationship with the people who create the works it publishes. It keeps identified records for authors and contributors (and their representatives, such as agents and literary estates), attributes them to the publisher's works with credited roles, records the contractual terms under which each work is published — rights granted, remuneration, payees and payment shares, advances — and operates the recurring settlement loop: sales data comes in, amounts owed to each author are computed under the contract's terms, statements are issued, and payments are tracked.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
Creator registry (identified authors/contributors — persons or organisations — plus representatives)
└── Work attribution (creator ↔ the publisher's works, with attributed roles)
    └── Contract record (per work: rights granted, remuneration, payees and shares)
        └── Settlement loop (sales intake → amount-owed calculation → statements → tracked payments)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — royalty escalators, reserves against returns, supply-chain contributor feeds, author self-service portals, rights-income tracking — is a standard capability layered on this spine, not part of what makes the software "author management." Older publishing operations ran the same four-part structure with card files, contract folders, and periodic royalty ledgers; modern products digitize it.

When the software's center of gravity shifts — to the work's bibliographic data rather than the money relationship, to the production lifecycle of titles, or to royalty recipients who need not be authors at all — it is functioning as a different Application Type (Publishing Metadata Management, Publishing Editorial Workflow, Royalty Management Platform).
definition.overview_zh:
一个**作者管理平台**是出版方软件，用于管理出版组织与创作其出版作品的人之间的持续关系。它为作者和贡献者（以及他们的代表，如代理和文学遗产）保留已识别的记录，将这些记录与出版作品以署名角色相关联，记录每部作品出版的合同条款——授予的权利、报酬、收款人和支付份额、预付款——并操作循环结算流程：销售数据流入，根据合同条款计算每位作者应得金额，发出账单，并跟踪支付。

定义核心有意保持较小：

```text
创作者注册表（已识别的作者/贡献者——个人或组织——加上代表）
└── 作品归属（创作者 ↔ 出版作品，带有署名角色）
    └── 合同记录（每部作品：授予的权利、报酬、收款人和份额）
        └── 结算循环（销售流入 → 应得金额计算 → 账单 → 跟踪支付）
```

与该类别通常相关的所有其他内容——版税阶梯、退货准备金、供应链贡献者 feed、作者自助服务门户、权利收入跟踪——都是叠加在此脊柱上的标准功能，不是使该软件成为“作者管理”的一部分。旧式出版运营使用卡片文件、合同文件夹和定期版税账本运行相同的四部分结构；现代产品将其数字化。

当软件的重心转移——从金钱关系转向作品的书目数据，转向书名的生产生命周期，或转向根本不是作者的版税接收者时——它作为不同的应用类型（出版元数据管理、出版编辑工作流、版税管理平台）运行。
definition.dc:
Four structures. Each answers a question the publisher must be able to answer at any time: *who are our authors, what did they write for us, on what terms, and what do we owe them?*

- **Creator registry** — every author or contributor is an identified record: a person or an organisation, with contact details, notes, and relationships. Records are shared across the whole system: the same record appears as the credited contributor on a work, the recipient of a statement, and a contact in the address book. Representatives — literary agents, estates — are typically records too, because they can be payment recipients without being credited contributors.
- **Work attribution** — creators are linked to the publisher's works (titles) with an attributed role ("author," "editor," "illustrator," "translator") and, commonly, a display order for public presentation. One person accumulates many work links over time; this accumulation is the author's history with the publisher.
- **Contract record** — for each work, the commercial terms of its publication: which rights the creator grants the publisher (often by territory), how remuneration is calculated (the royalty basis and rates), who the payees are and how the payment is divided among them, and what advances have been promised. Some products generate contract documents from this data; others store signed copies alongside structured terms. Either way, the terms exist as data, because the settlement engine consumes them.
- **Settlement loop** — the recurring operating cycle of the Type. Sales (and returns) data is imported from distributors and sales channels; amounts owed are computed per contract terms for the period; statements are produced per payee; payments are made and recorded; balances, advances, and held-back reserves carry forward to the next period.
definition.dc_zh: 四种结构。每种结构回答一个出版者必须随时能够回答的问题：*我们的作者是谁，他们为我们写了什么，在什么条款下，以及我们欠他们什么？*
definition.rules:
### The credited author and the payee are not necessarily the same record

Agents and literary estates commonly receive part or all of a work's royalty income. The system must therefore track, per work, *who is paid* separately from *who is credited* — the structural reason both concepts exist in every researched product.

### Rate rules are conditional and scoped

A work's royalty rate is rarely a single number: rates vary by edition/format, channel, territory, and by escalator conditions (units, value, time, discount). More specific rules override general ones. This is the machinery the contract record encodes and the settlement engine consumes.

### The settlement engine carries state forward

Advances paid, prior payments, and held reserves are not per-period events but running balances. A payment made outside a statement still needs to be recorded in the system, or the next period's balances will be wrong; reserves released in later statements supplement newly earned royalties. Statements are consequently cumulative documents, and mature products emphasize their auditability.

### Statements are per-payee, and their issue is a controlled event

Calculation results are reviewed before statements are finalized; the statement date fixes the period. Once issued, a statement is a financial document toward the author — products treat issue, delivery, and archiving as deliberate steps, not side effects.

### Public metadata is a contract-adjacent obligation

Credited roles and their order flow to the supply chain and shape how the world sees the author's contribution; some products carry the credited order into retail-facing feeds, because errors there are publicly visible and contractual-adjacent.

### Authors touch the system rarely — and on their own terms

Unlike employee-facing systems, the managed population is external. Self-service portals exist precisely because the relationship is intermittent: an author may interact only a few times a year, and the portal must make those interactions (statement lookup, contact update) staff-free.
definition.rules_zh:
### 署名作者和收款人不一定是同一条记录

代理和文学遗产通常接收作品的部分或全部版税收入。因此，系统必须分别跟踪每部作品的*收款方*和*署名方*——这是两个概念在每个研究产品中存在的结构性原因。

### 费率规则是有条件和范围的

作品的版税费率很少是一个单一数字：费率因版本/格式、渠道、区域和阶梯条件（数量、价值、时间、折扣）而异。更具体的规则覆盖一般规则。这是合同记录编码和结算引擎消耗的机制。

### 结算引擎将状态向前推进

已支付的预付款、先前支付和持有的准备金不是每期间事件，而是运行余额。在账单之外进行的支付仍需要记录在系统中，否则下一个期间的余额将出错；在后续账单中释放的准备金补充新赚取的版税。因此，账单是累积文档，成熟产品强调其可审计性。

### 账单是按收款人分的，其发出是受控事件

计算结果在账单最终确定前被审查；账单日期固定期间。一旦发出，账单是针对作者的财务文档——产品将发出、交付和归档视为有意步骤，而不是副作用。

### 公共元数据是合同相邻义务

署名角色及其顺序流向供应链，并塑造世界如何看待作者的贡献；一些产品将署名顺序带入面向零售的 feed，因为那里的错误是公开可见且合同相邻的。

### 作者很少接触系统——并且按照自己的条件

不像雇员

definition.name: Book Distribution Management
definition.overview:
A **Book Distribution Management** application is the operator-side system of record for running the distribution of published books into the book trade. It holds the publisher's or distributor's catalog of titles as sellable products, keeps trade customer accounts together with their commercial terms, takes and processes sales orders against stock, records dispatch and returns, and closes the operation into per-title, per-customer sales records that feed reporting, accounting, and royalties.

The defining core is small:

```text
Bibliographic title catalog (editions as identified, priced,
publication-stamped sellable products)
└── Trade customer accounts (book-trade buyers with commercial terms)
    └── Sales order binding titles × account × quantities
        └── Stock position per title that orders are fulfilled against
            └── Fulfillment / dispatch recorded as sales
               (title × account × quantity × value)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — ONIX metadata feeds to trading partners, EDI order exchange, returns and credit processing, sales analysis, print-on-demand linkage, digital channel distribution — is standard machinery of the book trade layered on that core, not what makes the system a distribution management system.

Two boundaries follow from this. The system is not the editorial/production side of publishing (acquisition, editing, production, contracts) — that is Book Publishing Management, although in the market the two frequently ship as modules of one publishing suite. And "distribution" here means the commercial and physical operation of selling and moving titles through the trade; the preparation and delivery of bibliographic *metadata* itself is a distinct concern (Publishing Metadata Management), even though metadata feeds are one of the standard capabilities of a distribution system.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**图书分销管理**应用是出版商或分销商用于管理已出版图书进入图书贸易流通的操作端系统记录。它存储出版商或分销商的书目目录作为可售产品，维护贸易客户账户及其商业条款，接收和处理基于库存的销售订单，记录发货与退货，并将运营数据汇总为按书目、按客户的销售记录，用于报告、会计和版税计算。

其核心定义结构十分精简：

```text
书目标题目录（已标识版本、定价、带有出版日期的可售产品）
└── 贸易客户账户（带有商业条款的图书贸易买家）
    └── 销售订单（绑定书目 × 账户 × 数量）
        └── 按书目区分的库存状况（用于履行订单）
            └── 履行/发货记录为销售
               （书目 × 账户 × 数量 × 价值）
```

通常与该类别相关的其他所有功能——向贸易伙伴提供ONIX元数据、EDI订单交换、退货和信用处理、销售分析、按需印刷对接、数字渠道分发——都是建立在这一核心之上的图书行业标准机制，并非使该系统成为分销管理系统的核心要素。

由此可界定两个边界。该系统并非出版流程中的编辑/制作环节（选题、编辑、制作、合同）——那属于**图书出版管理**，尽管市场上两者常作为同一出版套件的模块一同交付。此处的“分销”指的是通过贸易渠道销售和流转图书的商业与物理操作；书目*元数据*本身的准备和交付则是一个独立的关切点（**出版元数据管理**），尽管元数据推送是分销系统的一项标准能力。
definition.dc:
**Title / edition.** The central object is the bibliographic product: a specific edition of a work in a specific format, carrying its identifier (in practice an ISBN), format (print, e-book, audiobook), list price, publication date, and availability state. Editions of the same work are commonly grouped so that data shared across formats is maintained once. Every other object in the system refers back to titles; the catalog is what the trade buys.

**Trade customer account.** The buyers are accounts, not anonymous consumers: wholesalers, chains, independent bookstores, online retailers, library suppliers, and — for a distributor — the publishers whose titles it handles. An account carries its commercial standing: the discount structure applied against list price, the territories or markets it may buy for, payment terms, and contact details.

**Sales order.** An order binds specific titles to a specific account in quantities, at terms-derived prices. Orders arrive through trade channels — commonly EDI messages, account portals, or direct entry by staff — and are frequently processed in high volume. The order is the unit that drives the operational loop.

**Stock position.** Distribution means fulfilling orders from a stock position: physical stock in the operator's (or its fulfillment partner's) warehouse, and, increasingly, digital stock — e-book and audiobook entitlements delivered to platforms — plus print-on-demand as a supply mode that manufactures on order instead of holding stock. The stock position is what makes an order fulfillable or not.

**Fulfillment / dispatch and the sales record.** An accepted order is allocated against stock, dispatched (picked, packed, shipped — or triggered to a print-on-demand line, or delivered digitally), invoiced, and recorded as a sale: title × account × quantity × value. These sales records are the system's output to the rest of the business — sales analysis, royalty computation, and accounting all consume them.
definition.dc_zh:
**标题/版本。** 核心对象是书目产品：作品的特定版本（以特定形式呈现），承载其标识符（实践中为ISBN）、格式（印刷版、电子书、有声书）、定价、出版日期和可获得状态。同一作品的不同版本通常分组管理，以维护跨格式共享的数据。系统中的所有其他对象均指向标题；书目目录是行业交易的对象。

**贸易客户账户。** 买家是账户，而非匿名消费者：包括批发商、连锁书店、独立书店、在线零售商、图书馆供应商，以及对于发行商而言——其代理的出版商。账户包含其商业资质：基于定价的折扣结构、可采购的地区或市场、付款条款和联系方式。

**销售订单。** 订单将特定标题与特定账户按数量绑定，并根据条款确定价格。订单通过行业渠道（通常是EDI消息、客户门户或员工直接录入）抵达，且常以高容量处理。订单是驱动运营循环的单元。

**库存状态。** 发行意味着根据库存状态履行订单：包括运营商（或其履约合作伙伴）仓库中的实体库存，以及日益重要的数字库存——电子书和有声书的数字授权。
definition.rules:
**Publication date and availability gate the trade.** A title is not sold or shipped ahead of its publication state; availability data flows to the trade through the metadata feeds, and order fulfillment respects it. Where products combine formats, availability can differ per component.

**Price is list price minus terms.** The catalog carries list prices; what an account pays derives from its discount structure and territory. Terms changes propagate to order pricing; bulk price updates across the catalog are a standard operation.

**Orders are fulfilled against stock, not promises.** Allocation checks the actual stock position; unfulfillable demand becomes tracked backorders rather than silent promises. Fulfillment paths can mix warehouse stock, print-on-demand, and digital delivery.

**The trade runs on returnable stock.** Because much trade stock is sold on a returnable basis, every sale carries a potential reverse movement; returns reduce sales via credits and must reconcile against the original invoices. This makes the returns-and-credit cycle a first-class part of the operation, not an afterthought.

**Metadata quality is a gate, not a cleanup.** Trading partners consume title data automatically; systems therefore check completeness and validity before releasing feeds, and monitor feed delivery per destination.

**Sales records are attributed and reused.** Every recorded sale carries title, account, channel, period, and value — the substrate for sales analysis, royalty computation, and accounting. Attribution and audit trails matter because the same records settle money with authors and the trade.

**Access is role-governed.** Order entry, terms changes, price updates, and credit issuance are staff actions under permission control, with user attribution on financial records.
definition.rules_zh:
**出版日期与可用性决定贸易。** 书目不会在出版状态之前销售或发货；可用性数据通过元数据推送到贸易端，订单履行需遵守该状态。当产品组合多种格式时，可用性可能因组件而异。

**价格是定价减去条款。** 目录承载标价；账户支付价格源自其折扣结构和区域。条款变更会传播到订单定价；跨目录的批量价格更新是标准操作。

**订单基于库存而非承诺履行。** 分配检查实际库存状况；无法履行的需求成为可追踪的未交付订单，而非无声承诺。履行路径可混合使用仓库库存、按需印刷和数字交付。

**贸易基于可退货库存运行。** 由于大部分贸易库存按可退货方式销售，每笔销售都包含潜在的逆向流转；退货通过信用单减少销售，且必须与原始发票对账。这使得退货与信用循环成为运营的一等公民，而非事后补充。

**元数据质量是关口，而非事后清理。** 贸易伙伴自动消费书目数据；因此系统在推送前检查完整性和有效性，并按目的地监控推送交付情况。

**销售记录具有归属并可重用。** 每条销售记录都包含书目、账户、渠道、期间和价值——这是销售分析、版税计算和会计核算的基础。归属和审计跟踪至关重要，因为相同的记录用于与作者和贸易结算资金。

**访问受角色管控。** 订单录入、条款变更、价格更新和信用发放都是在权限控制下的工作人员操作，财务操作带有用户归属信息。

definition.name: Book Publishing Management
definition.overview:
A **Book Publishing Management** application is the publisher-side system of record for running the business of publishing books. It holds each title — a work together with its editions — as the central managed record, attaches the people who create it and the contracts that govern it, moves the title through a planned pre-publication lifecycle toward its publication date, and tracks the money and materials that surround it: the title's projected and actual profitability, its production schedules and manufacturing, its rights and permissions, the bibliographic metadata the trade consumes, and the sales data that flows back to settle what the publisher owes its authors.

The defining core is deliberately small:

```text
Title record (a work with its editions/products — the book as a
planned commercial product)
├── Contributors attached to the title under recorded contract terms
│   (attribution + rights granted + remuneration obligations)
└── Title lifecycle from pre-publication planning to publication
    (the record exists before the book is a certainty, and advances
    through planned stages toward a planned publication date)
```

Everything else commonly associated with the category — title P&L modeling, contract workflow, production scheduling, purchase orders, royalty settlement, ONIX metadata feeds, marketing collateral, seasons and backlists — is standard machinery layered on that spine, not what makes the software publishing management. A publisher that managed only titles, contributors-with-contracts, and publication plans — on paper or in a 1990s on-premise database — would be doing the same job this software digitizes.

Two boundaries frame the Type. It is a *business* management system, not the editorial content process itself and not a layout/typesetting tool. And it is the *publisher's* internal system: it ends where the trade operation begins (distribution), where the money relationship is isolated (author/royalty management), and where the ledger begins (finance/ERP).
definition.overview_zh:
**图书出版管理**应用程序是出版商侧用于运营业务的系统记录。它将每个书目——一部作品及其版本——作为核心管理记录，附加创建它的人员和规范它的合同，推动书目通过规划好的出版前生命周期走向其出版日期，并跟踪围绕它的资金和材料：书目的预计和实际盈利能力、生产计划和制造、权利和许可、行业使用的书目元数据，以及回流以结算出版商欠作者款项的销售数据。

其定义性核心刻意保持精简：

```text
书目记录（一部作品及其版本/产品——作为规划中商业产品的图书）
├── 根据已记录合同条款附加到书目的贡献者
│   （署名 + 授予权利 + 报酬义务）
└── 从出版前规划到出版的书目生命周期
    （记录存在于图书成为确定事实之前，并按规划阶段
    推进至计划的出版日期）
```

通常与此类别相关的其他所有内容——书目损益建模、合同工作流、生产排程、采购订单、版税结算、ONIX 元数据馈送、营销材料、季节性书目和库存——都是叠加在这个骨架上的标准机制，而非构成软件出版管理的本质。一家只管理书目、附带合同的贡献者和出版计划——无论是通过纸质还是1990年代的本地数据库——的出版商，所做的将是本软件数字化转型的同类工作。

两个边界界定了此类型。它是一个*业务*管理系统，而非编辑内容流程本身，也不是排版/版面工具。同时，它是*出版商*的内部系统：它终结于贸易运营开始之处（分销），资金关系被隔离之处（作者/版税管理），以及账簿开始之处（财务/ERP）。
definition.dc: The central object is the **title**: the book as a planned commercial product. Titles are commonly modeled in two layers — the **work** (the intellectual property: the novel, the biography, the textbook) and its **editions or products** (the specific sellable manifestations: hardback, paperback, e-book, audiobook, each carrying an identifier such as an ISBN, a format, a price, and a publication date). One work accumulates editions over time — an audio edition planned months after the print original, a revised edition years later — and mature products group these deliberately, so that data shared across formats is maintained once and version families can be navigated as a unit. Series and sets structure the catalog further.
definition.dc_zh: 核心对象是**书名（title）**：即作为规划商业产品的图书。书名通常被建模为两个层次——**作品（work）**（即知识产权：小说、传记、教科书）及其**版本或产品（editions or products）**（即具体的可售表现形式：精装本、平装本、电子书、有声书，每种都携带唯一标识符如ISBN、格式、价格和出版日期）。一个作品会随着时间积累不同版本——例如在印刷版发行数月后计划推出的有声版，或数年后推出的修订版——而成熟的产品体系会有意将这些版本进行分组，使得跨格式共享的数据只需维护一次，并且版本族系可以作为一个整体进行导航。丛书与套书进一步构建了产品目录的结构。
definition.rules:
**The record exists before the decision.** Titles are created as drafts during evaluation; a declined project is archived rather than deleted, because the evaluation work — data, contacts, models — is reusable and the audit trail matters. The live catalog only carries approved titles.

**The publication date gates everything.** Metadata-completeness and quality checks run before the date; the trade receives availability data keyed to it; schedules count down to it. A slipping date reschedules dependent tasks across departments — which is why the schedule is visible house-wide rather than private to production.

**Contract terms are data, not documents.** The settlement engine consumes structured terms — rates scoped by edition, channel, territory, escalators — so the contract record must be machine-readable even when signed documents are also stored. Advances are running balances with trigger events, not one-off entries.

**Origination costs attach to the work; manufacturing costs to the edition.** One copyedit and one typesetting are paid once for the work; each format carries its own print or digital production cost. P&L models and royalty rules both respect this split.

**Rights availability must be checked before selling.** What the publisher may exploit is bounded by what was acquired (scope, territory, duration); what it may sell is whatever it has acquired and not yet sold. Inbound permissions for third-party material are tracked with the same discipline, because unlicensed use carries legal exposure.

**Sales data returns and settles money.** Sales and returns reports flow back from the trade; the same records drive sales analysis, reprint decisions, and royalty computation. Attribution per title, channel, and period is required because the numbers settle contractual obligations.

**The title outlives publication.** Backlist management — reprints, new formats, price changes, continued royalties — is a first-class part of the model, not an afterlife. A title management system that forgot a book once published would stop being usable by any publisher with a catalog.
definition.rules_zh:
**记录存在于决策之前。** 书目在评估期间以草稿形式创建；被拒项目被归档而非删除，因为评估工作——数据、联系人、模型——是可复用的且审计线索很重要。正式书目仅包含已获批的书目。

**出版日期决定一切。** 元数据完整性和质量检查在该日期之前运行；行业获得以该日期为依据的可用性数据；排程倒计时至该日期。日期的推迟会重新安排跨部门的相关任务——这就是为什么排程在全公司可见，而非仅限于生产部门。

**合同条款是数据，而非文件。** 结算引擎使用结构化条款——按版本、渠道、地域、递增率划分的费率——因此合同记录必须是机器可读的，即使已签署文件也同时存储。预付款是带有触发事件的滚动余额，并非一次性分录。

**原创成本附属于作品；制造成本附属于版本。** 一次校对和一次排版为作品支付一次费用；每种格式有其独立的印刷或数字制作成本。损益模型和版税规则都遵循这一划分。

**销售前必须检查权利可用性。** 出版商可开发利用的权利受其获取范围（范围、地域、期限）限制；其可出售的权利则是已获取但尚未出售的部分。第三方材料的入站许可需以同样严格的纪律进行跟踪，因为未授权使用会带来法律风险。

**销售数据回流并结算资金。** 销售和退货报告从行业回流；同一记录驱动销售分析、重印决策和版税计算。按书目、渠道和期间进行归属是必需的，因为这些数字用于结算...
